mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the prior month's level coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its prior month's value by more than 0.25 percentage points
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative during FEDFUNDS tightening events, or the IC is > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below its 52-week low, equity discount rates are expected to normalize, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: In 80% of such events, 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market strengthening that boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by > 0.1 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: IC < 0.03 over 12 months, or 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive during such labor events (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a rebound above the prior month's level indicates improving supply conditions, which reduces near-term supply-side risks and supports positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO bounces back above prior month's value by > 2% after a > 3% monthly decline
failure_condition: Over 50 such bounces, 5-day forward returns are not positive (median negative).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises above 3% for two consecutive months, it triggers a preemptive rate hike anticipation that compresses equity valuations, producing negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 70% of such events, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in both retail sales (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) above their 5-year averages for three consecutive months predicts a robust demand environment that supports positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 5-year monthly avg AND INDPRO > 5-year monthly avg for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during 10 such events in the sample period.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in job openings reported by PAYEMS (two consecutive months below 7 million) combined with a sustained rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates softening labor demand, which is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 7 million for two consecutive months AND UNRATE rises by > 0.2 percentage points over the same period
failure_condition: During 30 such episodes, 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative (median non-negative).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in inflation-adjusted real yields (implied by a flattening of the 10-year Treasury yield relative to CPIAUCSL) over a 3-month horizon is associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as investors anticipate higher future earnings.
candidate_trigger: 10Y Treasury yield minus 12-month CPIAUCSL moving average declines by > 2 basis points over 3 months
failure_condition: Over 40 such 3-month declines, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (IC > 0.05).
